direction: Chalk & Concrete Brutalism — an editorial gym manifesto
rationale: Holdfast lives inside a RiNo warehouse where art, sweat, and concrete already coexist. Most climbing gym sites default to either moody adventure photography or chirpy SaaS-fitness. We split the difference with an editorial, almost zine-like brutalism: hand-scrawled chalk marks over slab-serif typography, route-tape color accents, and warm concrete neutrals. It signals 'serious climbing culture, zero attitude' — bold and a little irreverent like the voice, but warm enough that a first-timer feels invited, not gatekept.

palette.note: Warm concrete-canvas base (oklch ~0.92 0.02 80) with a route-tape orange primary (oklch ~0.66 0.18 38) and a chalk-yellow accent (oklch ~0.82 0.13 92). Tinted near-black foreground avoids the flat-digital tell. Mesh hero interpolates orange→clay→chalk in OKLCH so midpoints stay warm, never muddy.

fonts.display: Fraunces (variable, opsz pushed to 144, SOFT axis dialed down for slab edge)
fonts.body: Söhne Mono for eyebrows + Newsreader for paragraph
fonts.pairingNote: Fraunces at display sizes reads like a climbing magazine cover — slabby, confident, a little weird in its terminals. Newsreader keeps long-form readable and editorial; mono eyebrows nod to belay logs and route cards.

type.displayTreatment: Headlines set in Fraunces at clamp(3rem, 7.5vw, 7.25rem), line-height 0.94, tracking -0.04em. One word per hero headline gets a hand-drawn SVG chalk circle or underline (not a gradient). Eyebrows in mono UPPERCASE, 0.22em tracked, paired with a 40px hairline rule.
type.scaleNote: Aggressive 1.333 modular scale on desktop, compressed to 1.2 on mobile. Section numerals (01 / 02 / 03) set oversized in Fraunces italic at 8rem, bleeding off the left margin.

spacing.rhythmNote: Tone-band sections alternate concrete (#EFE9DF), chalk (#F6F1E7), and inverted slate (#1A1814). 160px vertical section padding on desktop, 96px mobile. Generous left-margin gutters echo a printed climbing zine.

motion.note: Section reveals fade + 24px rise, staggered 60ms, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1). The chalk-mark SVG underlines draw on with a 600ms stroke-dashoffset. Route-color tape strips slide in horizontally on the bento. Honors prefers-reduced-motion fully.

signatureDevices: OKLCH chalk-dust mesh hero: warm radial wash + one blurred clay orb + a single hairline horizontal rule at the baseline, overlaid with SVG fractalNoise grain at 0.04
Hand-drawn SVG chalk annotations (circles, underlines, arrows) layered over one word per headline — feels like a coach marking up a topo
Hairline-bento route-grade wall: 12-cell grid with 1px gaps on a foreground-tinted background, each cell tagged with a V-grade or YDS color stripe down the left edge
Oversized italic Fraunces section numerals (01–05) bleeding off the gutter, paired with mono eyebrows
Route-tape accent strips: 6px colored bars (the actual tape colors gyms use to mark routes) used as section dividers and CTA underlines instead of generic lines

imagery.direction: Real Holdfast members and staff — beginners chalking up, a kid topping out, a 50-ft lead climber mid-clip, the yoga studio at golden hour. Mix wide architectural shots of the warehouse bones (exposed brick, trusses, RiNo murals visible through the bay doors) with tight detail crops: chalked fingertips, taped knuckles, a shoe edging a foothold.
imagery.treatment: Duotone wash in concrete + clay (foreground/primary) for editorial sections; full-color reserved for the community/gallery wall where the RiNo personality earns it. Subtle film grain (0.03) over every image to match the page noise overlay.

voice: Direct, warm, a little smart-mouthed. Short declarative sentences. We say 'first climb's on us' not 'complimentary trial session.' We say 'you'll be sore tomorrow — in a good way' not 'transform your fitness journey.' We name things plainly: bouldering, ropes, auto-belays, the mezzanine, the yoga room. We never call climbers 'athletes' unprompted and we never, ever say 'crush it.'

sections.intent: OKLCH chalk-dust mesh background. Headline: 'Pull harder. Think less.' with a hand-drawn chalk circle around 'harder'. Mono eyebrow: 'RINO ART DISTRICT — EST. 2019'. Two CTAs: primary 'Book your free first climb' (orange with colored glow on hover), ghost 'Tour the gym'. Hours strip pinned bottom-left.

Asymmetric 2fr/1fr split: left holds a single declarative paragraph ('22,000 sq ft. 50-ft walls. 200+ routes reset every week. One very forgiving staff.'); right holds a hairline-bordered stat rail with four numbers (2,500+ members, 200+ routes/week, 50 ft of rope, 22k sq ft).

Hairline-bento of five tiles — Bouldering, Ropes & Lead, Auto-Belays, Fitness Mezzanine, Yoga & Movement — each with a route-tape color stripe and a 1-sentence plain-English description. Numbered 01–05 in oversized italic Fraunces.
Three-step horizontal sequence ('Show up', 'We hand you shoes', 'You climb something') with chalk-arrow SVGs connecting them. Sells the no-experience-needed promise without condescension.
Full-color (not duotone) masonry strip of member photos with first names and route names handwritten as captions. Links to Instagram.
Inverted slate tone band. Two-card comparison: Day Pass vs Membership, with the membership card carrying the orange accent and a 'most climbers pick this' chalk-circle tag.
Oversized Fraunces sign-off: 'First climb's on us.' with email capture and address/hours.
Eyebrow 'PRICING — NO TRICKS'. Headline 'Pay once a month. Climb whenever the doors are open.' Subhead names the freeze policy and no-initiation-fee thing up front.
Three plan cards (Adult, Student/Youth, Family) on hairline borders, each with route-tape color stripe. Feature list uses checkmarks drawn as small chalk ticks.
Secondary horizontal rail for Day Pass, 10-Punch, and Gear Rental — smaller type, mono pricing, signals these are options not the main path.
Accordion of the real questions: freezing, guest passes, cancellation, kids' age minimums. Answers in plain voice — 'Yeah, you can freeze for up to 3 months. Email us.'
Full-width inverted band: 'Still not sure? Climb free first.' with the free-first-climb booking link.
Headline 'Learn the ropes. Literally.' with chalk-underline on 'ropes'. Intro paragraph names the three tracks: Intro, Skills, Youth.
Three large bento cells — Intro to Climbing, Lead & Belay, Youth Team & Camps — each with a duotone photo, schedule snippet, and 'See dates' link.
Hairline-grid weekly calendar (Mon–Sun columns) showing recurring classes, yoga, leagues. Route-tape color codes by program type.
Coach roster as editorial cards: portrait (duotone), name, one-line bio in their own voice, favorite route grade.
Tone band promoting the seasonal league and monthly comps. Big italic numeral '04', short copy, RSVP link.
Architectural wide shot of the warehouse with headline 'A 22,000 sq ft playground inside a RiNo warehouse.' Eyebrow: '2500 LARIMER ST'.

Five stacked editorial spreads (one per space: Bouldering, Ropes, Auto-Belays, Mezzanine, Yoga Studio). Each spread is an asymmetric 7/5 split: oversized italic numeral + duotone photo on one side, plain-spoken description + stats on the other.
Story section about the setting crew — '200+ routes, fresh every week.' Includes a small calendar showing what got reset this week.
Hairline strip of practical stuff: showers, lockers, rental gear, coffee, kid-friendly hours, parking, transit.
Map embed styled in concrete tones + hours table + 'Book your free first climb' primary CTA.
Big Fraunces address block: '2500 Larimer St / Denver, CO'. Hours rendered as a hairline-bordered table, today's hours highlighted with the orange route-tape stripe.
Three short blurbs: driving + parking, light rail (38th & Blake), bike (the gym has racks). Honest, local, no fluff.
Plain-language checklist of what to bring and wear, plus what's included free (shoes on your first climb). Chalk-tick bullets.
Two-column: form on left (name, email, what's up), direct contact on right (hello@holdfast.demo, Instagram handle, a note that says 'a human responds within a day, usually faster').
